newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo central bank bonds interest rate at record low.
newsitem.headline: Yugo central bank bonds interest rate at record low.

text.p: Yugoslavia's central bank cut the interest rate on its short-term bonds auctioned on Friday to an annual 43.28 percent, the Belgrade bourse said.

The rate, corresponding to a monthly three percent, was the lowest since the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) first launched the instrument for regulating liquidity of the banking sector late in November 1995.
This compares to an annual 58.69 percent set for its previous tranche of bonds auctioned March 14.
The highest ever rate stood at an annual 147.48 percent and was set for the tranche auctioned January 13.

"The reduction is in line with the lower discount rate set at 2.5 percent per month for April but also to subdued inflationary pressures," head of the NBY Department for Open Market Operations Voja Scekic told Reuters.
The NBY sliced its key discount rate in March to 2.5 percent after keeping it at a monthly 4.5 percent for nine consecutive months.
Monthly inflation stood at 1.0 percent in March, slightly picking up after 0.6 percent in February.
A central bank analyst attributed the latest cut to an improved monetary stability.

"The NBY is holding a tight grip on monetary reins and creates no base money without hard currency backing. After some monetary distortions at the beginning of 1997, the situation has calmed and the NBY is entering the second quarter with more stability," said the source who asked not to be named.
"The central bank has no more reason to offer its securities with high interest," the source added.

The NBY offered for sale a new 30-million dinar ($5.41 million) tranche of its 30-day bonds, maturing May 4, but sold only 0.3 million dinars worth, the bourse said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
